item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 091715
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Fri Oct 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane Simon, located a
couple of hundred miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions are expected to
be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression is likely to form by late next week as the system moves
generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 50
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 091455
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  50
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM WATCHES ISSUED FOR SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA AND BAJA
CALIFORNIA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.8N 124.6W
ABOUT 935 MI...1505 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 820 MI...1325 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 55 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for the southern California
coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to the San Diego/Orange
County Line.
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Watch along the 
west coast of Baja California, from San Jose de Las Palomas 
northward to the U.S./Mexico Border and, the east coast of Baja 
California, from Isla San Luis northward to Puerto Penasco.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border
northward to the San Diego/Orange County Line
* West coast of Baja California, from San Jose de Las Palomas
northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in northern Baja California, northern Gulf of California, 
and Southern California should continue to monitor the progress of 
Rachel.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located near latitude 22.8 North, longitude 124.6 West. Rachel is 
moving toward the northeast near 5 mph (7 km/h). A general northeast 
to north-northeast motion, with a significant increase in forward 
speed is expected over the next couple of days. On the forecast 
track, the center of Rachel is expected to approach the northern 
Baja California Peninsula or southern California late Saturday 
or early Sunday.  
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some strengthening is possible the next day or two, with rapid 
weakening forecast after the storm moves inland over the 
southwestern United States on Sunday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header
WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch area 
in Baja California, and southern California by Saturday night or 
early Sunday. Strong gusty winds associated with the system are 
expected to spread over interior portions of the Southwest United 
States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from this weekend 
into early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of 
Baja California this weekend.

Rachel and associated moisture of the system will also bring 
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 
inches in portions of the Southwest United States this weekend. This 
will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for flash 
and urban flooding.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk 
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast 
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the 
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major 
coastal flooding, through early next week.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 AM PDT.
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 50
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 091456
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  50
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Satellite images indicate that Rachel is struggling to maintain deep 
convection, with only limited and shallow convection remaining near 
the center of circulation. A scatterometer pass received shortly 
after the previous advisory indicated peak winds of around 43 kt. 
Satellite intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 31 to 44 kt, 
while the TAFB subjective Dvorak estimate is T2.5/35 kt. Given the 
scatterometer data, the initial intensity is held at 45 kt for this 
advisory.

The storm is moving northeastward at an estimated 055/4 kt. A 
deepening mid-to upper-level trough moving into the eastern Pacific 
toward the western United States is expected to steer Rachel 
northeastward to north-northeastward with an increasing forward 
speed throughout the forecast period. On the forecast track, the 
system is expected to move inland over northern Baja California late 
Saturday or early Sunday before continuing northeastward into the 
southwestern United States on Sunday. There has been a northward 
shift in the latest track guidance, with the global and hurricane 
regional models now bringing the center near the U.S./Mexico border 
or into extreme southern California. The latest NHC track forecast 
has been nudged northward and lies between the global and regional 
hurricane models to the left, and the HCCA and GDMI slightly to the 
right. Given this track forecast, Tropical Storm Watches have been 
issued for portions of northern Baja California and southern 
California. There will be a sharp gradient in the wind field, with 
the strongest winds anticipated to remain primarily in the eastern 
and southern semicircles of the circulation.

Rachel remains embedded within a very dry air mass, with mid-level 
relative humidity values in the lower 30 percent range. Sea surface 
temperatures of around 24-25C will also limit convective 
organization. However, interaction with the aforementioned deepening 
trough is expected to increase mid-level moisture and improve 
upper-level divergence, allowing Rachel to produce intermittent 
bursts of deep convection and maintain tropical cyclone status. 
Furthermore, there are anomalously warm waters just offshore of 
northern Baja California for this time of year, running roughly 6-7C 
above normal. There has been a notable upward trend in the intensity 
guidance from the global and regional models this cycle, and the NHC 
forecast has been adjusted accordingly. As the system approaches the 
coast, increasing vertical wind shear is expected to displace the 
remaining convection downshear toward the northeastern portion of 
the circulation. Rachel is forecast to remain a strong tropical 
storm as it makes landfall. Once inland, rapid weakening is 
expected, and the system is forecast to become post-tropical over 
the southwestern United States. The latest NHC intensity forecast 
lies near the upper end of the guidance envelope, reflecting the 
complex interactions between Rachel and the approaching trough, as 
well as the inherent uncertainty in how models handle these 
processes.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of the northern Baja 
California Peninsula and southern California at tropical storm 
strength Saturday night, and a Tropical Storm Watch is now in effect 
from San Jose de Las Palomas, Mexico northward into southern 
California to the San Diego/Orange County Line. 

2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are 
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior 
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of 
higher terrain, Saturday night and Sunday.

3. Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will spread 
over portions of the Southwest United States and northern Baja 
California peninsula through this weekend. This will lead to 
increasing coverage of rainfall and for the potential of flash and 
urban flooding.

4. Swells partly generated by Rachel will continue to build along 
the coast of Southern California and northern Baja California.  
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major coastal 
flooding, through early next week.  Please consult products from 
your local weather office.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  09/1500Z 22.8N 124.6W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  10/0000Z 23.4N 123.6W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  10/1200Z 25.1N 121.0W   50 KT  60 MPH
 36H  11/0000Z 28.5N 118.1W   55 KT  65 MPH
 48H  11/1200Z 33.3N 116.0W   45 KT  50 MPH...INLAND
 60H  12/0000Z 38.1N 114.0W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 72H  12/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 9a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 091740
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 9A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
1200 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...SIMON FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY AND APPROACH THE COAST OF
MEXICO AS A DANGEROUS MAJOR HURRICANE THIS WEEKEND...
...PREPARATIONS SHOULD BE RUSHED TO COMPLETION TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.0N 104.7W
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 310 MI...500 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...973 MB...28.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Mita to San Blas
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 16.0 North, longitude 104.7 West. Simon is moving 
slowly toward the northwest near 2 mph (4 km/h). A gradual turn 
toward the north with a slight increase in forward speed is 
expected through tonight. Simon is then forecast to move 
generally northward, with the center passing very near or over the 
west-central coast of Mexico on late Saturday or Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Rapid strengthening is expected during the next day or so. 
Simon is forecast to become a major hurricane by this evening and 
strengthen further on Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80
miles (130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 973 mb (28.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area
Saturday evening or Sunday, with tropical storm conditions expected
Saturday morning.  Tropical storm conditions are possible within
the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning tonight or early Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 15
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 25 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
Jalisco and Nayarit through Sunday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is likely along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 091447
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
The intensity of Simon has been hard to diagnose this morning. The 
most recent TAFB Dvorak fix still supported an intensity of 80 kt 
at 1200 UTC, while all of the objective techniques from UW-CIMSS 
are lower. Since that time, a warm spot near the center of Simon's 
small CDO has recently appeared, which appears to be the early 
development of an eye. Based on the continued improvement in Simon's 
satellite appearance, the initial intensity has been increased to 85 
kt for the advisory.
 
Over the next 24 hours, continued rapid intensification is expected. 
The RI probabilistic guidance (both SHIPS and DTOPS) actually 
decreased this cycle, but the hurricane is located in a low-shear, 
high-moisture, and high-SST environment that is conducive for 
explosive deepening. Furthermore, recent microwave imagery, such as 
an AMSR3 pass just after 08Z suggests the hurricane has a small 
inner-core, which makes rapid changes in intensity more likely. 
Therefore, the NHC forecast is in line with the previous one, above 
most of the guidance and shows Simon becoming a major hurricane 
later today.
 
Simon's forecast beyond that is extremely difficult, and this is a 
case where it is important to not focus on the details of NHC's 
deterministic forecast. Simon will turn northward this weekend, 
steered between a deep trough to its northwest and a ridge to the 
east. This track will take the center of Simon very near or over the 
Mexican states of Colima and Jalisco. If the center of Simon moves 
over land, it will quickly weaken and could even dissipate, 
drastically lessening the risk of hurricane-force-winds farther 
north in Mexico. However, if the core of Simon remains offshore, it 
will likely continue northward as a hurricane. A majority of the 
guidance this morning shows Simon remaining just offshore, however 
most of these models have historically had a west bias in this 
region. Likewise, ensemble means like GDM or even HCCA can be 
misleading when some members move inland and dissipate. This 
results in the mean being computed solely from the surviving, and 
in this case farther west, members. The NHC forecast therefore 
remains within, but on the east side of the guidance envelope, and 
is best characterized as a hedge between the aforementioned 
possibilities. 
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico
as a major hurricane on Saturday.

2. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are 
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a 
Hurricane warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita. 
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by 
late today.

3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
